html:
Eva Perón, known as Evita, was the wife of President Juan Perón and the most powerful woman in Argentina from 1946 until her death in 1952 at the age of 33.

Born poor and illegitimate in the pampas, she moved to Buenos Aires at fifteen and became a radio actress. She married Perón in 1945. As first lady she ran a huge charity foundation that built hospitals, schools and homes, and she spoke to crowds of workers she called the descamisados, the shirtless ones. She led the campaign that won women the vote in 1947 and founded the women's Peronist party.

She died of cancer in 1952, mourned by millions. After the coup of 1955 her embalmed body was taken and hidden in Italy for sixteen years. To the poor of Argentina she is almost a saint; to her enemies she was a demagogue. The musical Evita made her known worldwide. Like the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo, she made women central to politics there.
